t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup drawn as an engineering drawing sheet on deep navy, inside a hairline zone-reference border with letters and numbers. A large light-weight off-white sans headline with thin steel-blue rules running out to both edges, and a warm limestone subhead. In the centre, a boxed hairline grid with small reference-code header cells and names for <CONTENT>. Hairline P&ID fragments, valves, a pump and dimensioned pipe bends, sit in the corners; a title block in the bottom right. Flat, square corners.
signature_idea: The review areas sit in a reference-coded grid on a navy drawing sheet ringed by P&ID fragments and a full title block.
strengths: richer drawing-sheet atmosphere than take 1, P&ID fragments add an engineering cue
steel-blue headline rules are a clean accent device
light headline and navy/limestone palette fit
weaknesses: grid is broken: empty cells, 'Sanitization' duplicated, header codes repeated and unrelated to rows
P&ID fragments are decorative and connect to nothing
title block text is garbled filler
headline is the page name, not the section; subhead carries the real title
busier and less calm than the brand wants; no mono type for codes
brand_fit_why: Palette, light type and square drawing-sheet frame fit, but duplicated garbled content, missing mono codes and decorative fragments break precision and calm.
